description: We are a team of six driven, intellectually curious students with a shared passion for science, technology, innovation and space exploration. Combining our diverse skills in programming, research, mathematics, design and creative problem-solving, we thrive on tackling ambitious challenges. Our NASA Space Apps Challenge project, MISSION: LEFT BEHIND, reflects our commitment to collaboration, innovation and turning ideas into reality.
summary: The project is an interactive space exploration game where players take control of a rover sent to explore the Moon and Mars. Along the journey, players discover traces previous space missions and abandoned equipment, uncovering the stories behind them. The game combines story-telling and problem solving to deliver an overall engaging and education experience. Through the immersive experience of controlling a rover, the project highlights the achievements of past missions, making space exploration and scientific discoveries more accessible and exciting for younger audiences.
details:
The Game

Players take control of a rover exploring the Moon and Mars environments. Every level consists of discovering clues that provide the player's rover with a new upgrade that allows them to unlock new areas to explore. The game consists of 4 main levels that provide these upgrades, and 6 mini games, totalling to 10 levels that teach the player about the equipment involved in each mission.

The mini games were designed to prevent gameplay from becoming repetitive, maintaining a balance between learning and entertainment.

The game was developed as a website so it is accessible on various devices. As it also includes educational material, hyperlinks of the resources used provide the user more information about the associated missions.

Ultimately, we aimed to create a game that makes players feel like real space explorers while teaching them about the incredible machines that helped humanity explore beyond Earth.

Games Preview

The Website

Alongside the interactive game, the website was split into another section, where users can find details of specific missions in an informative manner. The explore page allows users to engage with 3D models of the Moon and Mars, and pinpoint beacons where they can find out the key information about various missions.

A timeline provides mission information and links for more detail in order.

Artificial Intelligence Usage

We used OpenAI's ChatGPT as a development and creative assistant throughout the project.

AI helped us with:

  • Game development: Writing, improving and debugging code for the website, mini-games, 3D environments and rover upgrades.
  • UI/UX design: Developing layouts, interfaces, visual concepts and improving the overall user experience.
  • Problem-solving: Troubleshooting technical issues, improving gameplay mechanics and adapting the website for WordPress.

Our team’s contribution: We developed the project concept, selected the missions, decided on the features, guided the development process, provided feedback, and took responsibility for integration, testing and deployment. We also did the storyline and research.

NASA scientific data, historical photographs and videos were obtained from their original sources rather than generated by AI.

AI was used to assist development, while the team directed the creative and technical decisions

Note on Data and References

Since the majority of NASA data is linked within the website, the links on this page reference resources that are not explicitly included in our website's 'NASA Data & Resources' tab.
